description: Flying solo for my first Space Apps Challenge. Not an expert—just a computer science student curious to explore NASA's open data, test my programming skills, and build a working prototype from scratch
summary:
SPACE ECHOES is an interactive digital storytelling project that explores the stories of spacecraft, landers, rovers and scientific instruments that have completed their missions or become inactive in space. From the Moon to Mars and beyond, these forgotten explorers have left behind remarkable scientific achievements and historical footprints.

The project presents mission stories in an accessible and engaging way, helping people discover what these spacecraft accomplished, why their missions ended and where they remain today. It uses information from NASA's Space Science Data Coordinated Archive (NSSDCA) and other NASA resources to connect scientific data with human curiosity and space exploration history.

SPACE ECHOES aims to preserve the legacy of past space missions and inspire the next generation of explorers.
details: SPACE ECHOES is an interactive digital storytelling project that explores the history and legacy of abandoned and inactive space missions, focusing on the spacecraft and machines left behind on the Moon and Mars. The project works as a digital archive where users can explore different space missions, understand the original purpose of each spacecraft, discover its scientific achievements, learn why its mission ended, and understand what remains today. Through interactive mission stories, geographical filters, and educational information, SPACE ECHOES transforms space exploration history into an engaging learning experience. The project benefits students, educators, and space enthusiasts by making complex space science and historical mission information easier to understand while encouraging curiosity about astronomy, engineering, and planetary exploration. Its intended impact is to preserve the legacy of past space missions, spread awareness about their scientific contributions, and inspire the next generation to explore science and space technology. The project was developed using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, with HTML providing the structure, CSS creating the visual design, and JavaScript supporting interactive features. NASA's official mission information and space science archives were used as research references, and no specialised hardware was required. The creativity of SPACE ECHOES comes from presenting space exploration through the perspective of the machines that remained after their missions ended, turning scientific history into meaningful stories rather than simply listing facts. During development, we considered scientific accuracy, reliable sources, educational value, accessibility, simplicity, user engagement, and the importance of distinguishing historical facts from creative storytelling. Our ultimate goal is to show that even when a space mission comes to an end, its discoveries, achievements, and contributions continue to echo through the future of space exploration.
